documents.text: Married Women's Property Act 1870 The Married Women's Property Act 1870 (33 & 34 Vict. c.93) was an Act of Parliament of the United Kingdom that allowed married women to be the legal owners of the money they earned and to inherit property. Before 1870, any money made by a woman either through a wage, from investment, by gift, or through inheritance automatically became the property of her husband once she was married. source_segments.text: Married Women's Property Act 1870 The Married Women's Property Act 1870 (33 & 34 Vict.
c.93) was an Act of Parliament of the United Kingdom that allowed married women to be the legal owners of the money they earned and to inherit property.
Before 1870, any money made by a woman either through a wage, from investment, by gift, or through inheritance automatically became the property of her husband once she was married.
Thus, the identity of the wife became legally absorbed into that of her husband, effectively making them one person under the law.
